title: Zscaler Deception: decoys and lures, the Private Access integration, roles, and what can be automated

prose.text: Deception is an active-defense product with its own admin portal; it touches Private Access and Client Connector but is managed separately. {{what-it-is}} {{zte-response}}

prose.label: Deployment.
prose.text: {{deployment}} {{decoy-connectors}} {{portal-and-connector-components}} {{landmine-component}} {{zpa-integrated-containment}} {{zpa-no-extra-connectors}} Decoy Connector platforms, sizing and connection are in [[deception.decoy-connectors]], subnets and interfaces in [[deception.topology]], and the Landmine agents in [[deception.landmine-agents]] with their settings in [[deception.endpoint-settings]].

prose.label: Setup.
prose.text: {{configuration-guide-steps}} {{configuration-guide-siem-platforms}} {{configuration-guide-notification-scope}} Sign-in, users and roles, account settings and allowed IPs are in [[deception.admin-portal]], single sign-on in [[deception.sso]], and recommended deployments in [[deception.best-practices]].

prose.label: Decoys.
prose.text: {{decoy-types}} {{deceive-key-features}} {{strategy}} The attacker-facing MCP server decoy is in [[deception.mcp-server-decoys]]; what each plan includes is in [[deception.plans]]. The decoy types are in [[deception.network-decoys]], [[deception.ti-decoys]], [[deception.ad-decoys]], [[deception.gen-ai-decoys]], [[deception.cloud-decoys]], [[deception.landmine-policies]] and [[deception.landmine-decoys]], and Miragemaker and its datasets in [[deception.miragemaker]] and [[deception.datasets]]. Decoy deployment is in [[deception.decoy-deployment]].

prose.label: Detection and response.
prose.text: {{detect}} {{threatparse}} {{orchestrate-remediate}} Rules, actions and event templates are in [[deception.orchestration-rules]], containment integrations in [[deception.containment-integrations]], and Service Connectors in [[deception.service-connectors]]. The dashboard is in [[deception.investigate]], SIEM integrations in [[deception.siem-integrations]], enrichment integrations in [[deception.enrichment-integrations]], and the query syntax used in filters and conditions in [[deception.query-language]].

prose.label: Roles.
prose.text: {{roles}} Predefined roles, custom roles and users are in [[deception.admin-portal]].

prose.heading: What it changes in Private Access

prose.text: {{zpa-integration}} Objects Deception creates in Private Access are locked in the console: a Deception access rule's order cannot be updated and regular rules must order after it ([[zpa.policy.access-rule-order:deception-order-constraint]]), and Deception segment groups, connector groups, provisioning keys and log receivers cannot be edited or deleted ([[zpa.segment-groups.scope:deception-locked]], [[zpa.app-connectors.connector-groups:managed-read-only]], [[zpa.app-connectors.provisioning-keys:deception-managed-read-only]], [[zpa.log-receivers.admin-console:deception-readonly]]). {{mcp-zpa-skill}} The ZPA Terraform provider's handling of the rule named Zscaler Deception, which differs between v4.4.15 and v4.4.16, is in [[zpa.terraform.rule-order:configured-deception-rule-treated-as-unmanaged]] and [[zpa.terraform.rule-order:deception-offset-drift]].

prose.heading: What it changes in Client Connector

prose.text: Deception is a Client Connector service entitlement ([[zcc.entitlements:services-gated]]); a device's Deception settings OTP is `deceptionSettingsOtp` ([[zcc.passwords-and-otp.otp:otp-field-mapping]]), and the password that disables Deception is `zdpDisablePass` ([[zcc.passwords-and-otp.password-api:zad-zdp-names]]). {{mcp-zcc-otp}}

{{no-client-surface}} Token fields and expiry are in [[deception.api-tokens]]. API access exists in the product (Super admin manages APIs, and only the Advanced plan includes it: [[deception.plans:enterprise]]), but its endpoints and the lifecycle of the Private Access objects Deception owns are open {{gap:admin-api}}.

checks.do: Before changing Private Access policy order, segment groups, connector groups, provisioning keys or log receivers, whether the object was created by Deception, which the console treats as read-only.
For a Terraform plan that keeps renumbering access rules, which ZPA provider version is in use and whether a rule named Zscaler Deception sits at order 1.
Answer Deception automation questions as unsupported by any vendored client, and say that the product's API needs the Advanced plan and is not documented in any capture.

deceive-key-features.statement: Deceive configures and deploys decoys across public-facing endpoints, network, cloud and AD; its stated key features are stopping lateral movement, disrupting ransomware, detecting compromised users, detecting prebreach threats via TI decoys, and detecting enumeration activity and malicious access via AD decoy users.

quotes: Deceive allows you to configure and deploy decoys to disrupt active attacks, create fake attack paths, and gain high-fidelity threat intelligence.
You can deploy decoys across public-facing endpoints, network, cloud, and Active Directory (AD) to detect threats.
Stop lateral movement: Network decoys deployed in the network detect attackers attempting to move laterally and disrupt them.
Disrupt ransomware: Decoys placed across your environment detect and slow down ransomware at every stage of the kill chain and limit its blast radius.
Detect compromised users: Decoy passwords, cookies, sessions, and bookmarks to decoy applications detect compromised users when an attacker uses one of these deceptive assets.
Detect prebreach threats: TI decoys detect prebreach threats that specifically target your organization.
Detect enumeration activity and malicious access: Decoy users in an AD detect enumeration activity and malicious access.

what-it-is.statement: Zscaler Deception is a threat detection solution that uses lures and decoys to detect and disrupt sophisticated threats such as APTs, zero-day exploits, reconnaissance, lateral movement, and human-operated ransomware, and safeguards critical attack surfaces such as Active Directory, the software supply chain, and industrial control systems such as SCADA.

quotes: Zscaler Deception is a simple, faster, and more effective threat detection solution built on the Zscaler Zero Trust architecture.

Deception uses advanced lures and decoys to detect and disrupt sophisticated threats such as agentic attackers, advanced persistent threats (APTs), zero-day exploits, reconnaissance, lateral movement, and human-operated ransomware.

human-operated ransomware. By embedding these traps, the platform safeguards critical attack surfaces such as Active Directory, the software supply chain, and industrial control systems such as supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA).

zte-response.statement: As an integral part of the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange, Deception tracks the full attack sequence and initiates automated response actions across the Zscaler platform.

quotes: As an integral part of the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange, Deception integrates with Zero Trust, tracking the full attack sequence and initiating automated response actions across the Zscaler platform.

deployment.statement: Deception is cloud-delivered, needs minimal on-premises computing and no additional hardware upgrades.

quotes: Deception is cloud-delivered and scalable, and requires minimal on-premises computing. It does not require additional hardware upgrades.

decoy-connectors.statement: Network decoys are placed through Decoy Connectors connected to the Deception Admin Portal, with VLANs configured in the environment.

quotes: To place decoys on your network, Deception allows you to configure Decoy Connectors and connect them to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. You can configure virtual LANs (VLANs) in your environment to deploy network decoys.

zpa-integration.statement: Where Private Access (ZPA) is deployed, Deception can integrate with it to deploy Zero Trust Network decoys without installing additional network components or changing the network configuration.

quotes: If you have deployed Private Access (ZPA) for Zero Trust Network Access, you can integrate Deception with Private Access to deploy Zero Trust Network decoys without installing any additional network components or making any changes to your network configurations.

decoy-types.statement: Decoy types are network, Threat Intelligence (TI), Active Directory (AD), endpoint and cloud decoys; Miragemaker datasets make them more realistic.

quotes: You can configure and deploy network decoys, Threat Intelligence (TI) decoys, Active Directory (AD) decoys, endpoint decoys, and cloud decoys.
you can use the extensive datasets in Miragemaker to make decoys more realistic-looking and scalable.

strategy.statement: A Deception Strategy configures Network, TI and AD decoys and Landmine policies on one page from predefined personalities (built-in or custom strategies), and is deployed as Internal or Zero Trust Network (ZTN) decoys.

quotes: The Deception Strategy feature allows you to quickly configure Network decoys, Threat Intelligence (TI) decoys, Active Directory (AD) decoys, and Landmine policies on a single page.
A strategy consists of predefined personalities that are built based on different types of servers, applications, IT infrastructure, users, etc.
By default, Zscaler Deception provides built-in strategies that cover various business use cases to detect threats. You can create a custom strategy for your business needs.
After you create a strategy, you can deploy it using Internal or Zero Trust Network (ZTN) decoys.

detect.statement: When an attacker interacts with decoys, Deception collects the attacker's actions and intentions and generates high-fidelity, real-time alerts; because no legitimate traffic goes to decoys, any interaction is a high-confidence signal.

quotes: When an attacker infiltrates your network and interacts with the decoys, Deception detects threats, collects information on the attackers' actions and intentions, and generates high-fidelity and real-time alerts.
There is no legitimate business traffic to decoys, so any interaction with them is an immediate high-confidence signal of an ongoing breach

threatparse.statement: ThreatParse reconstructs attacks in natural language, summarizing log information in plain English to help the SOC and analysts understand what the attacker is trying to accomplish.

quotes: ThreatParse conducts natural language reconstruction of attacks, summarizes log information, and translates it into plain English to help the security operation center (SOC) and analysts understand what the attacker is trying to accomplish.

orchestrate-remediate.statement: Orchestration rules take immediate automated actions when events are discovered, and once an attacker's targets are known Deception deploys additional decoys to validate remediation.

quotes: Deception lets you orchestrate (automate) and build rules to take immediate actions when events are discovered to contain threats.
When the attacker's intended targets are uncovered, Deception deploys additional decoys to validate remediation.

roles.statement: Roles are Administrator (configures Decoy Connectors, deploys decoys, analyzes events, orchestrates actions), Analyst (investigates, blocks attackers, exports logs), Responder (analyzes events, orchestrates actions), Super admin (manages all features, including user roles, APIs, decoys and audit logs), and custom roles with chosen read and write permissions.

quotes: Administrator: Administrators can configure Decoy Connector (virtual machines), deploy decoys, view and analyze events, and orchestrate actions.
Analyst: Analysts can investigate events, block the attackers, and export logs.
Responder: Responders can analyze events and orchestrate actions.
Super admin: Super admins can view and manage all features and configurations of Deception, such as configuring user roles, APIs, decoys, audit logs, etc.
You can create a custom role with specific read and write permissions based on the requirements.

mcp-zpa-skill.statement: The MCP server's access-policy skill places a licensed Deception rule first in the order, as an auto-provisioned tenant feature whose default rule must not be modified.

quotes: | 1 | **A. Deception** (if licensed) | `ALLOW` | Predefined criteria | Tenant feature — auto-provisioned. Do **not** modify the default rule. |

mcp-zcc-otp.statement: The MCP server's ZCC OTP skill describes `deception_settings_otp` as the OTP that modifies Deception settings on the device.

quotes: | `deception_settings_otp` | Modify Deception settings on the device |

portal-and-connector-components.statement: The Deception standalone architecture's Admin Portal is a Zscaler-hosted cloud UI and central point of management and analysis that Decoy Connectors and software agents connect to; Decoy Connectors are virtual appliances that create decoys within trunked VLANs and can relay integrations to applications such as AD, SIEM and firewalls.

quotes: A cloud-hosted user interface (UI) hosted by Zscaler. It serves as the central point of management and analysis for the Deception service. Decoy Connector and software agents connect to it.
Lightweight virtual appliances that are hosted in your environment and can create decoy applications within multiple trunked virtual local area networks (VLANs) of your network.

Decoy Connectors can be used as a secure relay for integration between the Deception Admin Portal and applications, such as Active Directory (AD), security information and event management (SIEM), firewalls, etc. in your network.

landmine-component.statement: In the standalone architecture, the Landmine component is a software agent installed on endpoints such as desktops or laptops that deploys decoy credentials, files, processes, and lures to other decoys.

quotes: Landmine: Software agent installed on endpoints, such as desktops or laptops on your network. These agents deploy decoy credentials, files, processes, and lures to other decoys at your endpoints.

zpa-integrated-containment.statement: In the ZPA-integrated architecture, when an adversary breaks into the network and interacts with a decoy, Deception uses Zero Trust access policies to block the adversary's traffic to legitimate applications and contain the adversary to one system, building the picture from ZPA user and device identity; ZPA-based decoys are described as giving better visibility, intelligence and containment than non-ZPA decoys.

quotes: Decoys that make use of ZPA provide better visibility, intelligence, and containment capabilities than their non-ZPA counterparts.

When an adversary breaks into your network and interacts with a decoy, Deception leverages Zero Trust access policies to block traffic from the adversary to the legitimate applications and contains the adversary to one system.
Deception builds a complete picture of the adversary using the user and device identity information from the ZPA service.

zpa-no-extra-connectors.statement: With the ZPA integration, no additional Decoy Connectors or network configuration changes are needed to add deception to the environment, and the Landmine agent's lures direct adversaries toward decoy applications.

quotes: You don't have to install any additional Decoy Connectors or make any changes to your network configurations to add deception to your environment.

The Landmine agent deploys decoy credentials, files, processes, and lures to other decoys at your endpoints. These lures direct adversaries away from your legitimate assets and towards decoy applications.

configuration-guide-steps.statement: The step-by-step configuration guide lists six steps: log in to the Admin Portal, configure users and roles, optionally configure single sign-on, launch the deception campaign, configure SIEM integration, and configure alert notifications.

quotes: Step 1: Log In to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal
Step 2: Configure Users & Roles
(Optional) Step 3: Configure Single-Sign-On Authentication
Step 4: Launch Your Deception Campaign
Step 5: Configure SIEM Integration
Step 6: Configure Alert Notifications

configuration-guide-siem-platforms.statement: The configuration guide lists ArcSight, IBM QRadar, Microsoft Azure Sentinel, Netmonastery DNIF, Splunk, Syslog and Sumo Logic as supported SIEM integration platforms, configured through a Service Connector that forwards logs in real time.

quotes: You can configure a Service Connector to forward logs in real time.
Configuring SIEM integration for the following supported platforms:
ArcSight - IBM QRadar - Microsoft Azure Sentinel - Netmonastery DNIF - Splunk - Syslog - Sumo Logic

configuration-guide-notification-scope.statement: Email alert notifications can be configured per user and are sent when there is an issue with the decoys, license, or system, not when something happens on the decoys; Orchestrate rules can be added to create alerts when something happens on the decoys.

quotes: Notifications are sent to the user when there is an issue with the decoys, license, or system. Notifications are not sent if something happens on the decoys.
You can add Orchestrate rules to create alerts when something happens on the decoys.
You can configure the email alert notifications per user.

no-client-surface.statement: No vendored client manages Deception itself: the Go and Python SDKs, the Terraform providers, the Ansible collections, the MCP server and the OneAPI Postman collection mention Deception only through Private Access and Client Connector objects, not through decoys, strategies or alerts.

quotes: used in your server-side code to interact with the Zscaler API platform across multiple products such as:

no-client-surface.conditions: Rests on an absence. The Python README's product list (introduced by the quoted line) names no Deception API. At the pins, `git grep -i deception` finds only Client Connector OTP and password fields (Go, Python, ZCC provider), ZPA policy-order handling of the rule named Zscaler Deception (ZPA provider), and MCP skill text; the Postman matches are an EASM finding type (`DECEPTION_ENGAGED_CVE`) and a deception-method filter and field unrelated to the Deception product. No decoy, strategy, alert or orchestration endpoint appears.

admin-api.title: The Deception admin API, and the lifecycle of the Private Access objects Deception creates
admin-api.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the public captures do not identify the Deception admin API endpoints, its authentication model, the audit-log export contract, or the exact ownership boundary for Private Access objects created by Deception. Known: Super admin manages APIs (roles), API Access is an Advanced-plan feature (deception.plans:enterprise), and Private Access marks Deception-created objects read-only in the console. What the Private Access API does when such an object is changed is a separate gap: zpa.segment-groups.scope:deception-api-effect.
admin-api.blocks: automating decoys or alerts, and predicting what Private Access automation may change on Deception-owned objects
